mentions.name: Glyph
mentions.description: Glyph is a statically typed functional programming language in the ML family. Its surface syntax is mostly SML-1997-inspired, while underneath it uses simple-sub type inference, algebraic effects, modular implicits, and Perceus-style reference counting instead of a tracing GC. The compiler currently uses a Rust frontend, Zig codegen, and produces native binaries.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on Glyph, Its a is a statically typed functional language in the ML family.

Surface syntax is mostly SML-1997-ish, but underneath it's a different thing: simple-sub type inference, algebraic effects, modular implicits, and Perceus-style reference counting instead of a tracing GC.

The compiler is currently a Rust frontend -> Zig codegen -> native binary pipeline.
